Threat Hunting Methodology.description: Proactive threat hunting methodology to find undetected adversaries and improve detection coverage.

steps.task: Define hunt hypothesis — what TTP are you hunting for?
Reference MITRE ATT&CK for relevant techniques and data sources
Identify required data sources — are they available and complete?
Review recent threat intel — active threat groups targeting your industry
Define hunt scope — time range, asset groups, specific accounts
Document baseline — what does normal look like for this environment?
Verify log completeness — Sysmon, EDR, LDAP, DNS, proxy, firewall all ingesting?
Build baseline — typical process trees, network peers, logon patterns
Identify top talkers, beaconing patterns, high-volume LDAP accounts
Enumerate all service accounts — where do they authenticate from?
Identify DC-to-host replication — confirm all replication sources are DCs
Hunt for Kerberoasting — Event 4769, RC4 encryption (0x17) for non-machine accounts
Hunt for AS-REP roasting — Event 4768, PreAuthType=0
Hunt for DCSync — Event 4662 with DS-Replication-Get-Changes from non-DC
Hunt for Pass-the-Hash — Event 4624 LogonType=3 with NTLM auth from non-DC hosts; Event 4776 NTLM validation failures
Hunt for Golden/Silver Ticket — Event 4769/4768 TGS with no preceding TGT in same session; check for unusual EncryptionType or ticket lifetime >10h
Hunt for BloodHound collection — high-volume LDAP from single non-DC host; check Directory Service log or Sysmon Event 3 to DC port 389/636
Hunt for password spraying — Event 4625 (LogonType=3) across many accounts from one IP, or Event 4771 (FailureCode=0x18) from single source
Hunt for explicit credential abuse — Event 4648 from non-SYSTEM context; cross-correlate with lateral movement events 4624/5145
Hunt for delegation abuse — Event 4738 with TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION or DONT_REQ_PREAUTH; Event 5136 msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity modified
Hunt for LSASS access — non-standard processes opening LSASS handle (Event 10 Sysmon)
Hunt for LOLBin execution — mshta, regsvr32, certutil with unusual args (Event 4688 / Sysmon Event 1)
Hunt for PSExec artifacts — PSEXESVC service creation (System Event 7045; Security Event 4697 with actor attribution)
Hunt for WMI lateral movement — WmiPrvSE spawning cmd/powershell (Event 4688 parent=WmiPrvSE); Sysmon Event 19/20/21 for WMI subscriptions
Hunt for scheduled task persistence — Event 4698 (task created), 4700 (task enabled), 4702 (task modified); TaskScheduler/Operational Events 106/141/200
Hunt for AMSI bypass — specific PowerShell reflection patterns in Event 4104 script block logs (amsiInitFailed, AmsiUtils, amsiContext)
Hunt for encoded PowerShell — Event 4104, look for -enc / -encodedcommand; cross with 4688 parent process
Hunt for process injection — Sysmon Event 8 (CreateRemoteThread), Event 10 (ProcessAccess to lsass), Event 25 (process tampering/hollowing)
Hunt for BYOVD — Sysmon Event 6 (driver loaded from user-writable path or unsigned); cross with Event 7036/7040 security service stopped
Hunt for DLL side-loading/hijack — Sysmon Event 7 (image loaded from non-System32 path by signed binary); HKCU CLSID COM hijack (Sysmon Event 13)
Hunt for beaconing — regular outbound connections at fixed intervals (Zeek conn.log, NDR; Sysmon Event 3 periodic same-dest)
Hunt for DNS tunneling — high entropy subdomains, high TXT record query volume (Sysmon Event 22 / DNS debug log)
Hunt for C2 over uncommon ports — HTTPS on 8443, 4443, non-standard ports (Sysmon Event 3, firewall logs, Event 5156 WFP)
Hunt for data staging/exfil — large outbound transfers to new external IPs (proxy logs, firewall, DLP)
Hunt for SMB lateral movement — Event 5145 writes to ADMIN$/C$; Event 5140 share access from unusual hosts; internal port 445 Sysmon Event 3
Hunt for LDAP enumeration — >1000 LDAP queries from workstation in short window (Directory Service log; Sysmon Event 3 to DC:389)
Hunt for named pipe C2 — Sysmon Event 17/18 (pipe create/connect); check for Cobalt Strike default pipe names (postex_, msagent_, MSSE-)
Hunt for CloudTrail anomalies — API calls from new geo/IP, unusual regions
Hunt for IAM abuse — policy attach, role creation, new admin users
Hunt for IMDS exploitation — credential requests from unexpected instances
Hunt for Azure AD impossible travel — sign-ins from 2+ locations in <1hr
Hunt for legacy auth sign-ins in Azure AD (SMTP, IMAP, POP3 — MFA bypass)
Hunt for mass S3/GCS/Blob download activity
Hunt for SUID abuse — unusual SUID binary execution by non-root user
Hunt for LD_PRELOAD injection — env var set before command execution (auditd)
Hunt for reverse shells — /dev/tcp, nc -e, socat, python pty in bash history
Hunt for PAM backdoor — pam_permit.so or unusual entries in /etc/pam.d/
Hunt for cron persistence — new cron entries by non-root in /etc/cron.d or /var/spool/cron
Hunt for credential theft — /etc/shadow reads, SSH key access by unexpected process
Hunt for history clearing — HISTFILESIZE=0, history -c, unset HISTFILE
Hunt for binary execution from /tmp, /dev/shm, /run/user — common dropper locations
Document all queries used, data sources, and time range
Record findings — confirmed threats, suspicious activity, or clean
Convert successful hunt queries into permanent detection rules
Identify detection gaps found during hunt — log sources missing?
Share hunt report with SOC team and leadership
Update threat hunting hypothesis backlog with new ideas
